label: Avatar
title: Avatar
summary: Represent one person or account with an image or initials.
corePrinciple: Use a real image when available; use a short monogram otherwise.

anatomy.title: A circular frame holds an image or initials
anatomy.description: Avatar keeps the outer size and shape while its content style changes. The markers point to the real component instance.
blocks: Avatar Size sets the token-owned width and height; its default radius resolves to a circle.
The Monogram style centers the supplied text and uses Avatar label tokens.
The Image style crops a supplied image source into the same circular frame.

anatomy.note: Avatar Size sets the token-owned width and height; its default radius resolves to a circle.
The Monogram style centers the supplied text and uses Avatar label tokens.
The Image style crops a supplied image source into the same circular frame.

configuration.title: Choose Image or Monogram
configuration.description: Style selects which content is rendered. Monogram uses its text property; Image uses imageSource and otherwise shows the package fallback.
blocks: Provide an image source that represents this person. The bundled fallback is only a preview when no source is supplied.
Use a short, recognizable set of initials when a portrait is not available.

states.title: Loading preserves the selected size
states.description: Loading is a runtime state supplied through SkeletonGroup, not a style or size variant. It replaces the identity content with a same-size neutral placeholder.
blocks: The image or monogram remains inside the chosen Avatar Size.
The token-backed Skeleton circle is expected while the image or monogram is unavailable.

sizing.title: Pick one of the four Avatar Size modes
sizing.description: The modes resolve to token-owned dimensions. A surrounding card or row can provide room, but it does not stretch Avatar automatically.

content.title: Avatar content is an image or monogram text
content.description: Set Style to Image or Monogram, then supply the matching image source or monogram text.
blocks: Supply initials for a compact text based identity.
Set imageSource to the intended image.
The XS example shows a single monogram letter.

inContext.title: Identify an account owner at a glance
inContext.description: A surrounding Card may add a name or role when the layout calls for it; Avatar does not require nearby text.
blocks: The Card adds optional context outside Avatar.

doDont.title: Give every identity meaningful content
doDont.description: The repeated fallback looks like one person even when it is used for several different accounts.
blocks: Use a portrait or clear initials
Each Avatar shows its own portrait or monogram content.
Reuse the built-in fallback for different people
Both images resolve to the same bundled fallback and cannot distinguish separate identities.

do.title: Use a portrait or clear initials
do.caption: Each Avatar shows its own portrait or monogram content.

dont.title: Reuse the built-in fallback for different people
dont.caption: Both images resolve to the same bundled fallback and cannot distinguish separate identities.

sources.title: Use the public style, text, image, and size choices
sources.description: The guide compares the exposed Figma property with the installed package and the canonical published stories.
blocks: Public component master and exposed properties
Docs page and public example behavior

The declared and installed jfs-components version is 0.1.60; the earlier registry check on 23 September also returned 0.1.60. A fresh registry lookup could not be confirmed during recovery because registry DNS was unavailable. Figma exposes Image and Monogram plus monogram text; Storybook also demonstrates size and remote-image examples. Supply a person-specific imageSource; the package fallback is only a preview. Loading replaces Avatar content with a neutral, token-backed Skeleton inside an active SkeletonGroup. This version drops its typed accessibility label and keeps role image on the press wrapper, so examples remain non-interactive.
